title: The back-rank mate

card.idea: A king tucked behind three untouched pawns is safe from nearly everything, except a rook or queen landing on his own back rank. He has no square to step to, so the check is mate. The same hole is sitting in your position too.
card.habit: Give your king a square to breathe.

explain.text: The black king on g8 has f7, g7 and h7 filled by his own pawns. Rd8 checks him along the eighth rank and there is nowhere at all to go: mate. The pawns that keep him safe from the side are the same pawns that trap him.

Here Black has pushed the h-pawn to h6, so the king has h7 to step to and a check on the back rank is only a check. One quiet pawn move is the whole defence. Look at your own back rank before somebody makes you look at it.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square the black king can move to.

hints.text: His own pawns stand on f7, g7 and h7, so forget that whole row.
hints.text2: Only the back rank is left, and only two squares of it.

wrong.Rd7: Close, but that only attacks the pawns. The empty rank behind the king is the one that matters.

challenges.reason: The eighth rank is empty apart from the king, and his own pawns take away every square in front of him.
The queen does a rook's job here: she checks along the eighth rank and the pawns on f7, g7 and h7 do the rest.

wrong.Ra7: That hits the pawns but gives no check. Go all the way to the back rank.

challenges.reason: The a-file is clear all the way up, and the king on f8 is walled in by e7, f7 and g7.

challenges.prompt: Mate in one. Your own back rank is thin too, so do not dawdle.
challenges.reason: Qb8 checks along the eighth and g7 and h7 are his own pawns. Note that Black was one move from doing the same thing to you.

challenges.prompt: Black's rook is eyeing your back rank. Tap the square your king will be able to step to once the h-pawn goes to h3.
challenges.reason: Moving the h-pawn up one opens h2 for the king, and a check on the first rank is then only a check.

hints.text: The pawn that moves is the one on h2, so ask what it leaves behind.
hints.text2: Your king needs a square on the second rank, on the edge.

challenges.prompt: White has just played Rb8. What has happened?
options: Check, but the king steps to h8

hints.text: Ask where the king could go. His own pawns are on f7, g7 and h7.

takeaway: Three pawns in front of your king keep him safe and keep him trapped — give him a square.
